simple.meaning: מֶמְשָׁלָה (memshâlâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “rule ; also (concretely in plural) a realm or a ruler.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 15 times across Genesis, 1 Kings, 2 Chronicles, Psalms, Isaiah, and 3 more, beginning at Genesis 1:16. Its contexts include kingship, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מֶמְשָׁלָה (H4475).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מֶמְשָׁלָה (memshâlâh) / H4475 is traced through Genesis 1:16, 1 Kings 9:19, 2 Chronicles 32:9, Psalms 103:22 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: rule ; also (concretely in plural) a realm or a ruler
definitions.full: H4475. memshalah מֶמְשָׁלָה noun feminine rule, dominion, realm (compare Dr Jphil. xi. 1882, 215 ); — absolute ׳מ Micah 4:8 ; construct מֶמְשֶׁ֫לֶת Psa 136:8 (before בְּ Ges § 130 , 1 Kö ii. 182 ), Jer 34:1-2 t.; suffix מֶמְשַׁלְתְּךָ Isa 22:21 ; Psa 145:13 ; מֶמְשַׁלְתּוֺ 1Kin 9:19 6 t.; plural construct מֶמְשְׁלוֺת Psa 136:9 ; suffix מַמְשְׁלוֺתָיו 114:2 ; — 1 rule, dominion (human) Isa 22:21 ; Micah 4:8 ; עִמּוֺ מֶמְשַׁלְתּוֺ וְכָלֿ 2Chr 32:9 and all his imperial might with him (i.e. display of might — soldiers, court, luxury, etc.; of Sennach.); מֶמְשַׁלְתּוֺ אֶרֶץ כֹּל 1Kin 9:19 2Chr 8:6 ; Jer 51:28 , יָדוֺ מֶמְשֶׁלֶת אֶרֶץ מַמְלְכוֺת 34:1 ; hence ׳מ alone = relam, domian 2Kin 20:13 = Isa 39:2 ; Dan 11:5 . 2 rule of heavenly bodies ׳לִמְשׁ הַיּוֺם Gen 1:16 the sun for the rule ofthe day , compare 1:16 ; also followed by בְּ Psa 136:8 ; 136:9 . 3 God's rule dominion: Psa 145:13 (|| מַלְכוּת ), מֶמְשַׁלְתּוֺ כָּלמְֿקֹמוֺת 103:22 ; plural = realm ׃ מַמְשְׁלוֺתָֽיו יִשְׂרָאֵל לְקָדְשׁ֑וֺ יְהוּדָה הָֽיְתה 114:2 . I, II. מִשְׁמָע , [ מִשְׁמַ֫עַת ] see שׁמע . מִשְׁמָר , [ מִשְׁמֶ֫רֶת ] see שׁמר . מִשְׁנֶה see שׁנה . מְשִׁסָּה see שׁסס . משׁע (compare Assyrian misû , cleanse , wash , compare Dl HWB ; whence might come following — though שׁ = s is surprising — compare Dl Baer, Ezech. xiv ).

occurrences.englishText: God made the two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night. He also made the stars.

After this, Sennacherib king of Assyria sent his servants to Jerusalem, (now he was before Lachish, and all his power with him), to Hezekiah king of Judah, and to all Judah who were at Jerusalem, saying,

the sun to rule by day;

and I will clothe him with your robe, and strengthen him with your belt. I will commit your government into his hand; and he will be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to the house of Judah.

Hezekiah was pleased with them, and showed them the house of his precious things, the silver, the gold, the spices, and the precious oil, and all the house of his armor, and all that was found in his treasures. There was nothing in his house, nor in all his dominion, that Hezekiah didn’t show them.
